```{r}
visit_counts <- table(visits_per_patient)

barplot(
  visit_counts,
  main = "Completed Appointments per Patient (Preliminary)",
  xlab = "Number of completed appointments",
  ylab = "Number of patients",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = NA
)
```
Of 44 customers IDs with qualifying completed appointments, 17 have one record and 27 have two or more. Most 31 of 44 have one or two, while a few have much higher counts, which include two with 36 each. 

This shows how common repeat visits are and how visits are distributed across patients. The preliminary repeat proportion is 61.4%, but possible test accounts and duplicate records could inflate it. It is not yet a validated retention rate.

Appointment records peak in May 2024, with 83 records. 

This helps determine whether high appointment volume reflects many different patients or repeated activity from a few IDs. The May spike is concentrated, so it should not yet be interpreted as increased demand. Months with zero qualifying records are omitted from this chart.

```{r}
visit_dates <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT customer_id, appointment_date
  FROM appointments
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND appointment_outcome = 'visit complete'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND appointment_date IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY appointment_date
")

dates_by_patient <- split(
  visit_dates$appointment_date,
  visit_dates$customer_id
)

days_to_second <- sapply(dates_by_patient, function(dates) {
  if (length(dates) < 2) return(NA_real_)

  as.numeric(difftime(dates[2], dates[1], units = "days"))
})

summary(days_to_second)

hist(
  days_to_second[!is.na(days_to_second)],
  main = "Time to Second Completed Appointment (Preliminary)",
  xlab = "Days between first and second appointments",
  ylab = "Number of patient IDs",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = "white"
)
```
Among the 27 repeat IDs, the median gap between their first two observed appointment is 14.3 days. A few long gaps raise the mean to 69.7 days. 

This addresses how soon patients return, which adds information beyond simply counting visits. However, minute-long gaps require review, and the chart excludes IDs without an observed second appointment. 

```{r}
sum(days_to_second < 1, na.rm = TRUE)

short_gaps <- days_to_second[!is.na(days_to_second) &
                               days_to_second < 1]

unname(round(short_gaps * 24, 2))
```

```{r}
satisfaction_available <- c(
  Recorded = sum(!is.na(
    satisfaction$patient_interaction_satisfaction
  )),
  Missing = sum(is.na(
    satisfaction$patient_interaction_satisfaction
  ))
)

barplot(
  satisfaction_available,
  main = "Satisfaction Data Availability (Preliminary)",
  ylab = "Number of appointment records",
  col = c("steelblue", "gray70"),
  border = NA
)
```
Satisfaction is recorded for 61 of 219 appointments records (27.9%) and missing for 158 (72.1%). 

This chart shows a major limitation when comparing satisfaction between one-time and repeat patients: that comparison would cover only a minority of records and could be biased if ratings are recorded selectively. Also, 33 recorded values are zero. This chart shows data availability, not whether patients are satisfied.

```{r}
report_links <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    r.id AS report_id,
    r.customer_viewed_date,
    o.customer_id
  FROM resultvalues AS r
  LEFT JOIN samples AS s
    ON r.hormone_sample_id = s.id
  LEFT JOIN shipments AS sh
    ON s.shipment_id = sh.id
  LEFT JOIN orders AS o
    ON sh.order_id = o.id
  WHERE r.customer_viewed_date IS NOT NULL
")

nrow(report_links)
length(unique(report_links$report_id))

sum(is.na(report_links$customer_id))
```

“How should we identify real, completed patient visits and exclude internal testing, duplicates, or rescheduled appointments?”
We found test-like comments, conflicting completion labels, and appointments minutes apart. A reliable visit definition is essential for calculating visits per patient and repeat visits.

“What is the correct way to link a patient’s report-viewing date to their first appointment booking, and which timestamps should we use?”
This directly supports your goal of measuring the share of report viewers who book a visit and how long that takes. We need to confirm that the linked customer is the patient and that booking occurred after viewing.

“Where is follow-up recommendation information recorded, and how should we interpret the satisfaction fields?”
The follow-up flag is missing for all 219 qualifying records, and many satisfaction values are missing or zero. Clarifying these fields will help you assess whether follow-up recommendations and satisfaction are associated with repeat visits.

```{r}
count_patient_visits <- function(data) {
  counts <- aggregate(
    id ~ customer_id + visit_type,
    data = data,
    FUN = length
  )

  names(counts)[3] <- "visit_count"
  return(counts)
}

patient_counts <- count_patient_visits(completed_visits)

with(patient_counts, table(visit_count, visit_type))
```

```{r}
visit_span <- function(dates) {
  dates <- dates[!is.na(dates)]

  if (length(dates) < 2) return(NA_real_)

  return(as.numeric(
    difftime(max(dates), min(dates), units = "days")
  ))
}

patient_spans <- aggregate(
  x = list(span_days = completed_visits$appointment_date),
  by = list(
    customer_id = completed_visits$customer_id,
    visit_type = completed_visits$visit_type
  ),
  FUN = visit_span
)

with(patient_spans, tapply(span_days, visit_type, summary))
```

```{r}
satisfaction_visits$score_status[
  blank & satisfaction_visits$visit_type %in%
    c("15-minute video", "25-minute video")
] <- "Missing"

] <- "Not expected"

with(
  satisfaction_visits,
  table(visit_type, score_status)
```

```{r}
label_satisfaction <- function(data) {
  data$score_status <- "Recorded"

  blank <- is.na(data$patient_interaction_satisfaction)

  data$score_status[blank] <- "Expectation unknown"

  data$score_status[
    blank & data$visit_type %in%
      c("15-minute video", "25-minute video")
  ] <- "Missing"

  data$score_status[
    blank & data$visit_type == "Async"
  ] <- "Not expected"

  return(data)
}

satisfaction_visits <- label_satisfaction(satisfaction_visits)

with(satisfaction_visits, table(visit_type, score_status))
```

```{r}
get_report_waits <- function(reports, bookings) {

  matched <- merge(reports, bookings, by = "customer_id")

  matched$days_to_booking <- as.numeric(
    difftime(
      matched$created_date,
      matched$customer_viewed_date,
      units = "days"
    )
  )

  later <- subset(matched, days_to_booking >= 0)

  # Keep the earliest later booking for each report
  later <- later[order(later$days_to_booking, later$id), ]
  first <- later[!duplicated(later$report_id), ]

  # Include reports with no later booking
  result <- merge(
    reports,
    first[, c("report_id", "id", "sku", "days_to_booking")],
    by = "report_id",
    all.x = TRUE
  )

  return(result)
}
```

```{r}
get_transitions <- function(data) {

  data <- subset(data, !is.na(appointment_date))

  data <- data[
    order(data$customer_id, data$appointment_date, data$id),
  ]

  data$next_type <- ave(
    data$visit_type,
    data$customer_id,
    FUN = function(x) c(x[-1], NA_character_)
  )

  data$next_date <- ave(
    as.numeric(data$appointment_date),
    data$customer_id,
    FUN = function(x) c(x[-1], NA_real_)
  )

  # Exclude tied times because their order is uncertain
  transitions <- subset(
    data,
    !is.na(next_type) &
      next_date > as.numeric(appointment_date)
  )

  return(transitions)
}

transitions <- get_transitions(completed_visits)

# Display counts for each sequence
transition_table <- with(
  transitions,
  table(visit_type, next_type)
)

knitr::kable(
  transition_table,
  caption = "Consecutive completed visit types — staging data"
)
```

## Virtual Care and Repeat Visits Analysis 

1. Preparation Code 

```{r}
library(DBI)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

care_appointments <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT id, customer_id, appointment_date, created_date,
         status, appointment_outcome, sku,
         patient_interaction_satisfaction
  FROM appointments
")

care_reports <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT r.id AS report_id,
         r.customer_viewed_date,
         o.customer_id
  FROM resultvalues AS r
  LEFT JOIN samples AS s
    ON r.hormone_sample_id = s.id
  LEFT JOIN shipments AS sh
    ON s.shipment_id = sh.id
  LEFT JOIN orders AS o
    ON sh.order_id = o.id
  WHERE r.customer_viewed_date IS NOT NULL
")
```

```{r}
prepare_care <- function(data) {
  data |>
    mutate(
      visit_type = case_when(
        sku == "VC-SYNC-15CHRG" ~ "15-minute video",
        sku == "VC-SYNC-25CHRG" ~ "25-minute video",
        sku %in% c("VC-ASYC-ADCHRG", "VC-ASYC-ADFREE") ~ "Async",
        TRUE ~ "Unknown"
      )
    )
}

care_appointments <- prepare_care(care_appointments)

care_completed <- care_appointments |>
  filter(
    status == "completed",
    appointment_outcome == "visit complete",
    !is.na(customer_id)
  )
```


2. Visit Counts and Time Spans 

Question: How many completed visits does each distinct customer have, 
and how much time do these visits cover within each type?

```{r}
care_span <- function(dates) {
  dates <- dates[!is.na(dates)]

  if (length(dates) < 2) return(NA_real_)

  as.numeric(difftime(max(dates), min(dates), units = "days"))
}

care_median <- function(values) {
  if (all(is.na(values))) return(NA_real_)

  median(values, na.rm = TRUE)
}

count_care_visits <- function(data) {
  data |>
    group_by(customer_id, visit_type) |>
    summarise(
      visit_count = n(),
      span_days = care_span(appointment_date),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

care_counts <- count_care_visits(care_completed)

care_count_summary <- care_counts |>
  group_by(visit_type) |>
  summarise(
    customer_ids = n(),
    completed_visits = sum(visit_count),
    repeat_customer_ids = sum(visit_count >= 2),
    ids_with_usable_span = sum(!is.na(span_days)),
    median_span_days = round(care_median(span_days), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(care_count_summary)
```

```{r}
plot_care_spans <- function(data) {

  usable <- data |>
    filter(!is.na(span_days))

  ggplot(usable, aes(x = span_days, y = visit_type)) +

      color = "#3182BD",
      size = 3,
      alpha = 0.7,

        "Small vertical offsets help separate overlapping dots.",
        sep = "\n"
      )
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}

plot_care_spans(care_counts)
```


3. Completed Visits Per Customer 

Question: Are customers represented mostly by one visit or by repeated visits? 

```{r}
plot_care_frequency <- function(data) {
```

4. Time Between Visits (First-To-Second and Second-To-Third Gaps) 

Question: How much time passes between repeat visits? 

```{r}
care_gap <- function(dates, visit_number) {
  dates <- sort(dates[!is.na(dates)])

  if (length(dates) < visit_number) return(NA_real_)

  as.numeric(
    difftime(
      dates[visit_number],
      dates[visit_number - 1],
      units = "days"
    )
  )
}

calculate_care_gaps <- function(data) {
  data |>
    group_by(customer_id, visit_type) |>
    summarise(
      first_to_second = care_gap(appointment_date, 2),
      second_to_third = care_gap(appointment_date, 3),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

care_gaps <- calculate_care_gaps(care_completed)

care_gap_summary <- care_gaps |>
  group_by(visit_type) |>
  summarise(
    ids_with_first_gap = sum(!is.na(first_to_second)),
    median_first_gap_days = round(care_median(first_to_second), 3),
    ids_with_second_gap = sum(!is.na(second_to_third)),
    median_second_gap_days = round(care_median(second_to_third), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(care_gap_summary)
```

```{r}
plot_care_gaps <- function(data) {

  first <- data |>
```

5. Report Viewing To First Subsequent Booking 

Question: How long after viewing a report was the first subsequent 
appointment record created, and what type was it?

```{r}
get_care_report_waits <- function(reports, appointments) {

  matched <- merge(
    reports,
    appointments[, c("customer_id", "id", "created_date", "visit_type")],
    by = "customer_id"
  )

  first_bookings <- matched |>
    mutate(
      days_to_booking = as.numeric(
        difftime(
          created_date,
          customer_viewed_date,
          units = "days"
        )
      )
    ) |>
    filter(days_to_booking >= 0) |>
    arrange(days_to_booking, id) |>
    distinct(report_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(report_id, id, visit_type, days_to_booking)

  merge(
    reports,
    first_bookings,
    by = "report_id",
    all.x = TRUE
  )
}

care_waits <- get_care_report_waits(
  care_reports,
  care_appointments
)

care_waits |>
  summarise(
    viewed_reports = n(),
    with_later_booking = sum(!is.na(days_to_booking)),
    without_later_booking = sum(is.na(days_to_booking))
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

care_waits |>
  filter(!is.na(days_to_booking)) |>
  group_by(visit_type) |>
  summarise(
    reports = n(),
    median_wait_days = round(median(days_to_booking), 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

7. Video Visits Followed by Async Care

Question: Do async visits happen after unknown video visits, and how long 
afterward? 

```{r}
get_care_async_gaps <- function(data) {

  video <- data |>
    filter(visit_type %in% c("15-minute video", "25-minute video")) |>
    select(customer_id, id, appointment_date, visit_type)

  async <- data |>
    filter(visit_type == "Async") |>
    select(customer_id, id, appointment_date)

  pairs <- merge(
    video,
    async,
    by = "customer_id",
    suffixes = c("_video", "_async")
  )

  pairs |>
    mutate(
      gap_days = as.numeric(
        difftime(
          appointment_date_async,
          appointment_date_video,
          units = "days"
        )
      )
    ) |>
    filter(gap_days > 0) |>
    arrange(gap_days, id_video) |>
    distinct(id_async, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

care_async_gaps <- get_care_async_gaps(care_completed)

care_async_summary <- care_async_gaps |>
  group_by(visit_type) |>
  summarise(
    async_visits = n(),
    customer_ids = n_distinct(customer_id),
    median_gap_days = round(median(gap_days), 2),
    shortest_gap_days = round(min(gap_days), 2),
    longest_gap_days = round(max(gap_days), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(care_async_summary)
```

```{r}
label_care_satisfaction <- function(data) {
  data |>
    mutate(
      score_status = case_when(
        !is.na(patient_interaction_satisfaction) ~ "Recorded",
        visit_type == "Async" ~ "Not expected",
        visit_type %in%

        TRUE ~ "Expectation unknown"
      )
    )
}
```
